extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling U.S. ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, examiner practices, and filing/serving rules for conducting U.S. ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including handling responses, defective papers, service, timing, supplemental responses, and revival petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide reply requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s or patent owner’s reply must appear throughout to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or the reexamination proceeding to final action. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the language of the claims patentably distinguishes them from the references does not comply with the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must specifically point out patentable distinctions over applied references; boilerplate assertions of patentability are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment must point out patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: In amending in reply to a rejection of claims in an application or patent under reexamination, the applicant or patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty which he or she thinks the claims present in view of the state of the art disclosed by the references cited or the objections made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant or patent owner must also show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch and applicable examination provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte reexamination proceedings, including appeals to the Board, will be conducted with special dispatch within the Office. After issuance of the ex parte reexamination order and expiration of the time for submitting any responses, the examination will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.104 through 1.116 and will result in issuance of an ex parte reexamination certificate under § 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutive timelines and procedures per cited sections apply; expedite processing is a statutory mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum response period for patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally patent owner is given a period of 2 months to respond; extensions only as authorized by rule § 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of patent owner response to rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to any rejection, such response may include further statements and/or proposed amendments or new claims to place the patent in a condition where all claims, if amended as proposed, would be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should aim to place claims in condition for allowance if possible; consider proposed claim amendments and supporting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time — cause and petition fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for taking any action by a patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Any request for such extension must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due, and must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g). Mere filing of a request does not effect any extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 1.304(a) for extensions relating to appeals or civil actions; late or unsupported extension requests will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failure to file timely response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under § 1.560(b), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution, and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under § 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination is automatic unless delay is excused via petition under § 1.137 (unavoidable) or accepted as unintentional under § 1.137(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse for delayed response (unavoidable or unintentional)
rubrics_metrics.description: The delay in filing a response may be excused if it is shown to the satisfaction of the Director that the delay was unavoidable (petition under § 1.137(a)), or the response may nevertheless be accepted if the delay was unintentional (petition under § 1.137(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must comply with § 1.137(a) or (b) respectively and include required showing and fees where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement on other party
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided by § 1.248. The document must reflect service or the document may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a certificate of service indicating name, address, and method of service; include copy of certificate with the served copy. Lack of proof of service may result in refusal to consider the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of requester participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535, and no further submissions on behalf of the reexamination requester will be acknowledged or considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further submissions from requester are not considered unless in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535 or entered into the file prior to the order under § 1.525.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions after order must meet §1.501(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by third parties filed after the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525 must meet the requirements of and will be treated in accordance with § 1.501(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations filed solely on patents/publications after the order are typically delayed to storage until proceedings conclude (see § 2206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirements for ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(6) except for specified exceptions (e.g., certain extension petitions, petitions to accept delayed responses under § 1.137(b), petitions under § 1.78, and petitions under § 1.530(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the listed exceptions carefully before submitting a petition without fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental response entry conditions (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2), a response that is supplemental to a response that is in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right. The Office may enter a supplemental response if the supplemental response is clearly limited to specified categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed supplemental response categories include: (A) cancellation of claim(s); (B) adoption of examiner suggestions; (C) placement of the proceeding in condition for Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC); (D) response to a requirement made after the first response was filed; (E) correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); or (F) simplification of issues for appeal. Entry is subject to examiner cursory review and timing (must be entered before examiner considers prior response).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unentered supplemental response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental response which has not been approved for entry will not be entered when a response to a subsequent Office action is filed, even if there is a specific request for its entry in the subsequent response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner wishes the unentered supplemental response considered, the contents must be included in a proper response to the subsequent Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing third-party papers by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must not file papers on behalf of a third party. If a third party paper accompanies or is submitted as part of a timely filed response, the response and the third party paper are considered improper and will be returned to the patent owner; the third party paper will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When returning an improper submission, the decision should provide an appropriate extension under 37 CFR 1.550(c) to refile the patent owner response without the third party paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) prohibited in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner cannot submit an application data sheet (ADS) in a reexamination proceeding since a reexamination proceeding is not an 'application' (see 37 CFR 1.76). An ADS is an improper paper in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include ADS in reexamination filings; such submissions may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'not fully responsive' to non-final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A response by the patent owner will be considered not fully responsive to a non-final Office action where: (A) a bona fide response to an examiner’s non-final action is filed; (B) before the expiration of the permissible response period; (C) but through an apparent oversight or inadvertence, some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category is limited to inadvertent omissions, not deliberate omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner options for not fully responsive submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent owner submission is not fully responsive to a non-final Office action but meets the inadvertent-omission criteria, the examiner may: (A) waive the deficiencies (if not serious) and act on the submission; (B) accept the amendment as a response but notify the owner via a new Office action setting a new time period for response; or (C) notify the owner that the response must be completed within the remaining period for response (or extension) to avoid termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option (C) used only when there is sufficient time remaining in the response period (including authorized extensions). Examiner should exercise discretion and avoid creating abuse for delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when submission contains minor deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patent owner’s submission responds to the rejections, objections, or requirements and is a bona fide attempt but contains a minor deficiency (e.g., fails to treat every rejection), the examiner may simply act on the amendment and issue a new (non-final or final) Office action that identifies the omitted part and clarifies what is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Office action may indicate omitted rejection is reiterated or no longer applicable; examiner must identify specific unaddressed parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling serious omissions or insufficient time
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission contains a serious deficiency to be dealt with prior to issuing action on the merits and the period for response has expired, or there is insufficient time remaining, the patent owner should be notified of the deficiency and given a new time period for response (usually 1 month). The patent owner must supply the omission within that new period (or authorized extensions) to avoid termination under 37 CFR 1.550(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice is analogous to 37 CFR 1.135(c) for applications; failure to supply within new period risks termination of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened period to correct omissions (Form paragraph 22.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.14 may be used where a bona fide response is not entirely responsive to a non-final Office action. A shortened statutory period for response to this letter is set to expire ONE MONTH, or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from the mailing date of this letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should explain in bracket 2 the nature of the omitted point and what is needed to complete the response. The paragraph is only used for pre-final responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice limited to inadvertent omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving the patent owner a time period to supply an omission in a bona fide response applies only when the missing matter or lack of compliance is considered by the examiner as being 'inadvertently omitted.' Deliberate omissions do not qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once inadvertence is brought to owner's attention, it no longer exists; repeated use to gain time may be abused and should be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final responses and advisory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving time to supply an omission does not apply after a final Office action. If a bona fide response after final rejection omits a necessary point, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; rather, an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) should be issued with explanation of omission. Time set in the final rejection continues to run and is extended by 1 month if the response is the first after final in accordance with MPEP § 2265.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or better form for appeal; otherwise denied entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion including Ex parte Quayle action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner has authority to enter the response, withdraw the final Office action, and issue a new Office action (which may be final), or close prosecution in an otherwise allowable application under Ex parte Quayle, if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must weigh that substantial patent rights are at issue and that patent owner may lack opportunity for refiling; exercise discretion carefully when prosecution time has expired and an amendment would place the proceeding in condition for issuance but for an inadvertent omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects making paper an 'informal submission'
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if substance is complete, the submission can be defective (an 'informal submission'). Examples of defects include: (A) paper does not include proof of service; (B) paper is unsigned; (C) paper is signed by a non-practitioner who is not of record; (D) the amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) the amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form PTOL-475 to notify defects; include additional explanation on separate sheet when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and correction period for defective papers (PTOL-475)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a submission made prior to final rejection is defective, form PTOL-475 is used to provide notification of defects. A time period of one month or thirty days, whichever is longer, from the mailing date of PTOL-475 will be set for correction of the defect(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension may be requested under § 1.550(c). If defect not corrected, submission will not be entered and may lead to termination if it causes failure to file a timely and appropriate response.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final defective responses handled by advisory action
rubrics_metrics.description: If a defective (informal) response to an examiner’s action is filed after final rejection (before expiration of permissible response period), the examiner should not issue a PTOL-475; rather, issue an advisory Office action (PTOL-467) explaining the defect. Time in final rejection continues to run and may be extended by 1 month as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2265 and § 2272 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service details and consequences of omission
rubrics_metrics.description: As proof of service, the party submitting the paper must attach a certificate of service to the paper including the name and address of the party served and the method of service. A copy of the certificate must be attached with the copy served on the other party. Any paper filed without proof of service may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proof is omitted, Central Reexamination Unit should contact submitter to determine if actual service occurred; if not, the submission may be placed in the IFW file history as an unentered paper with 'N/E' notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to effect service
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure of a party to serve the submission in response to the notice will have consequences: (A) For a patent owner statement or a third party reply, the submission may be refused consideration. (B) For a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration and prosecution may be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d), unless the patent owner has otherwise completely responded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and proper service is essential to preserve consideration of submissions and avoid termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of inappropriate or untimely papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers found inappropriate because of defects will either be returned or discarded at the Office's option, or forwarded to one of three files: 'Reexamination File', 'Patent File', or 'Storage File'. Papers returned by CRU or TC must be accompanied by a letter indicating signature and approval of the CRU or TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return of inappropriate submissions reduces scanning and preserves public record integrity; certain returns require Director approval or referral to Patent Legal Administration when accompanied by petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of papers returned (owner/requester/third party)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: (Owner) Premature responses filed prior to an order to reexamine will be returned and not considered; papers submitted on behalf of a third party will be returned. (Requester) Reply when owner failed to file a statement is inappropriate and will be returned; late requester responses (>2 months from service) will be returned; additional requester responses beyond § 1.535 reply will be returned. (Third party) Unsigned papers or papers without proof of service may not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be limits on iterations of party input to honor statutory mandate for special dispatch. Opposition to petitions (rare) must be filed within two weeks to ensure consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage file placement for late third-party citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by third parties based solely on prior art patents or publications filed after the date of the order to reexamine are not entered into the patent file but delayed (placed in 'Storage File') until the reexamination proceedings have been concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly and timely filed third-party citations (filed prior to the order) are placed in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival fees for petitions to revive delayed responses
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing each petition for the revival of an unintentionally delayed response by the patent owner in any reexamination proceeding, the revival fee is $1,620 (unless petition filed under sections 133 or 151 where the fee is $540).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory fee under 35 U.S.C. 41; ensure correct fee code and statutory basis when filing revival petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.137 revival petition requirements (unavoidable vs unintentional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the delay in reply was unavoidable, a petition under § 1.137(a) may be filed to revive a reexamination prosecution terminated under §§ 1.550(d) or 1.957(b) or limited under § 1.957(c). Grantable petition must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee as set forth in § 1.17(l); (3) a showing that the entire delay was unavoidable; and (4) any terminal disclaimer required. For unintentional delay, § 1.137(b) applies with its own requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully document and support the showing of unavoidable or unintentional delay and include required fees and any terminal disclaimer.
